title: Nairobi Water Sets 26-Hour Supply Shutdown Across Nairobi
desc: Nairobi Water will shut down the Sasumua plant for 26 hours from Friday, affecting Eastlands, Mathare, South B, CBD and other parts of Nairobi.
content:
The Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company has announced a 26-hour water supply interruption across several parts of Nairobi as emergency repairs are carried out along the Sasumua-Kabete pipeline.

In a notice issued on Thursday, September 10, Nairobi Water said the scheduled shutdown of the Sasumua Water Treatment Plant will begin at 6:00 a.m. on Friday, September 11, and run until 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 12.

The company said the shutdown is necessary to facilitate emergency repair works along the Sasumua-Kabete pipeline and advised customers in affected areas to prepare before the interruption begins.

“Customers are strongly advised to store adequate water in advance and use available supplies sparingly,” Nairobi Water said in the notice.

The disruption will affect a wide section of the capital, including Eastlands and its surrounding areas.

In Eastlands, the listed areas include Eastleigh, Maringo, Buruburu Phases 3 and 4, Gikomba, Pumwani, Majengo, Shauri Moyo, Jericho, Jerusalem and Kimathi.

Other heavily populated areas listed include Mathare, Huruma and the Outer Ring corridor. The affected locations in this section include Mathare North, GSU, Rafiki, Mlango Kubwa, Juja Road, Huruma, Ngei I and II, Kosovo, Racecourse, Ushirika, parts of Ngumba Estate and Baba Dogo, among others.

The interruption will also affect the entire Industrial Area, including Masai Road and adjacent areas.

Other parts of Nairobi named in the notice include Westlands, Lavington, Kileleshwa, Kilimani, Hurlingham, Upper Hill, Dagoretti, Kawangware, Waithaka, Uthiru, Mutuini and Gatina.

Residents in Kibera, Langata, Nairobi West, Madaraka, South B, South C and Jamhuri are also expected to experience the interruption.

The CBD, parts of Mombasa Road, JKIA, the SGR corridor, Embakasi, Imara Daima, Tassia and Mukuru are among other areas listed by Nairobi Water.

The company also included parts of Ngara, Gigiri and the diplomatic area, including Village Market, UNEP and the US Embassy.

For households and businesses, the 26-hour shutdown could affect cooking, cleaning, sanitation and other activities that depend on a reliable water supply. Businesses such as eateries, salons, laundries and other water-dependent enterprises may also need to make arrangements before the shutdown.

Nairobi Water's advice means residents in the affected areas should store enough water before 6:00 a.m. on Friday and use available supplies carefully during the interruption.

The scheduled shutdown is expected to end at 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 12, after which water supply should resume as the network is restored.
